If you've ever put an OpenAI, Claude or Gemini key into a hosting or bot service, set a spending cap at the provider and swap the key if that service reports a breach.

items.headline: OpenAI buys Odessia, an AI travel agent, hinting at trip planning in ChatGPT
items.explainer: Odessia planned and booked trips with AI, and its founder Francis Davidson (who started Sonder) now works on travel at OpenAI. OpenAI hasn't announced a travel product, and Odessia's own service has already shut down, so anyone who used it should save their trip details elsewhere.

items.headline: ElevenLabs' Scribe v3 transcribes speech with 27% fewer mistakes and better 'who said what'
items.explainer: Meeting-note apps and voice bots built on ElevenLabs should get cleaner transcripts in 102 languages, better speaker labels with three or more people, and a live version that doesn't cut you off when you pause mid-number. It's the default in the ElevenLabs app now, and developers switch by changing one model name.

items.headline: Spotify's AI DJ gets nine new voices and a switch to stop the chatter between songs
items.explainer: Premium listeners can pick from seven new English voices and two Spanish ones, and turn off the commentary so the music just plays. Find it by searching DJ in the app and tapping the three-dot menu.

items.headline: Otter's AI notetaker adds 13 languages now and 14 more soon, at no extra cost
items.explainer: Mandarin, German, Italian, Korean, Portuguese and others work today for transcripts, summaries and action items, and a coming mode will follow a meeting as people switch languages. Otter says it runs its own speech models, so your audio isn't sent to another AI company.

items.headline: Google's top model, Gemini 4 Carbon, is now open to paying developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers
items.explainer: Carbon is Google's strongest model for long, multi-step jobs like big coding projects, research and security work, and it's now in the Gemini API for every paying developer at $2 in / $10 out per million tokens until Nov 30 ($4 / $20 from Dec 1), plus the Gemini app, AI Mode and Antigravity for Ultra subscribers. It uses more tokens than Gemini 4 Argon to think things through, so Google still points most everyday work to Argon; Antigravity also gets a /swarm preview that turns one prompt into a team of agents.

items.headline: Claude can now build spreadsheets and whiteboards with you, and open apps like Notion or Adobe right beside the chat
items.explainer: Ask for a budget or a tracker and Claude makes a real sheet with tabs, formulas and drop-downs you can edit together and export to Excel or CSV; Whiteboards turns a messy plan into a board with owners and dates (both beta on paid plans), and Claude Data (formerly Dashboards) is now generally available. Anthropic also announced Claude Meetings, which joins Google Meet calls as a visible participant for Team and Enterprise plans, and connected apps can now open full-size so Claude can make changes in them while you approve each action.

items.headline: Businesses can now claim a profile in ChatGPT, and some US shops can add their own chat agent
items.explainer: When ChatGPT mentions a business you may now see its verified profile and, for eligible US online stores and services, a clearly labeled Business Agent you can ask about products. That agent speaks for the business, not for you, and some can be sponsored placements, so double-check claims; OpenAI says businesses don't see your chats, only aggregated numbers.

items.headline: n8n releases Nod, a free open-source agent that runs errands on your own Mac or Windows PC
items.explainer: Nod works in its own sandbox and browser on your computer, so it can cancel a subscription, watch a price or download monthly invoices, and it checks with you before it sends, pays, posts or deletes anything. It's a research preview: you bring your own AI provider (API key or ChatGPT plan) and pay for that usage, it asks once a task passes $5, and it stops when your laptop sleeps.

items.headline: Adobe puts its Creative Agent across Firefly and Creative Cloud and previews a way for outside agents to edit your Photoshop files
items.explainer: You can describe a multi-step edit in Firefly, Premiere, Illustrator or InDesign and the assistant (beta) does it, and new always-on agents (preview) can sort incoming files or prep content in the background. A local MCP preview will let agents like Claude or ChatGPT make changes inside your Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects files while keeping layers editable; 9to5Mac reports that part arrives in 2027.

items.headline: eBay appears to be blocking AI agents like Meta's Muse from browsing its listings
items.explainer: If your bot used to pull eBay deals into a daily digest, it may now come back empty or send you to copycat sites; eBay says it restricts agent access in some cases and already banned agents that buy without a person reviewing the order. Amazon also blocks outside agents, so check the store's own app or alerts when your bot hits a wall.

items.headline: Anthropic starts its IPO roadshow, aiming for $70 to $78 a share on Nasdaq as ANT
items.explainer: Claude's maker plans to sell about 825 million shares, so the listing is close but the shares aren't sold yet. Nothing changes in Claude for you today; once public, Anthropic has to report its business openly, which can shape prices and plans later.

items.headline: Skills, reusable instructions for Gemini, are rolling out across Gmail, Docs, Slides, Drive and Chat for work accounts
items.explainer: You write your team's rules, templates and reference files once as a skill, and Gemini applies it automatically when it fits or when you @mention it; skills can also kick off Workspace Studio automations. It uses the same open SKILL.md format as other AI tools, so you can copy instructions between them by hand; Rapid Release domains get it first and Scheduled Release domains from Nov 30.

items.headline: You can now see, fix and delete what Gemini remembers about you
items.explainer: A new Memory summary page (Settings > Personal Intelligence on the web) lists what Gemini has learned about you by topic, and you can type 'remove my old phone number' or 'add that I speak Japanese' to change it, plus see a history of changes. It's for US English Google AI subscribers for now; worth a two-minute check if you share personal details with it.

items.headline: A breach at AI vendor Fireworks exposed some Notion AI chat transcripts
items.explainer: Fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces were affected and most chats had no names attached, but Notion says to treat them as exposed and change any password or API key you pasted into Notion AI. It's a reminder that what you type into an AI tool can pass through other companies, so keep secrets out of chats.

items.headline: Apple starts selling $49.99 packs of extra AI use, starting in Logic Pro
items.explainer: It's Apple's first charge for extra Apple Intelligence use: Creator Studio subscribers who hit the monthly limit on features like the Logic Pro assistant can buy a one-time pack that rolls over and expires after 12 months. It isn't shareable with family or refundable, so check Show Usage before buying; Apple Intelligence on your phone is still free.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent now works on Apple Watch and Wear OS watches
items.explainer: You can call Muse, text it or dictate a request from your wrist, and Apple Watch gets a watch-face shortcut, so you can hand it a quick errand like a booking or a calendar clash without pulling out your phone. The Apple Watch app is a companion to the iPhone app (watchOS 9 or later), Meta hasn't listed which Wear OS watches work, and since Muse can reach your email and calendar, only connect what you're comfortable with.

items.headline: Google Antigravity gets a simpler Knowledge Work layout for research and writing, not just coding
items.explainer: The same agent, models, plugins and connectors are there, but the Git, terminal and code-diff clutter is hidden and permission prompts are described in plain words. Personal Google accounts can switch in Settings, General, Interface Layout (version 2.30.0); business and enterprise accounts stay on the developer layout, and voice mode is now rolled out to everyone else.

items.headline: OpenAI built Control Room, an internal off switch that halts research AI jobs within 35 seconds
items.explainer: It covers OpenAI's own training and testing work, not the ChatGPT you use, and it blocks a flagged job's model output even if the job itself keeps running. It's a sign labs are adding hard stops as agents get more capable.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2, its top model, 20% cheaper and up to 30% faster
items.explainer: Claude's most capable generally available model gets better at coding, reasoning and vision, and is built to run long projects and teams of agents. It's out today on all platforms at $8 / $40 per million tokens (down from $10 / $50), eligible paid Claude plans get extra Fable usage this week, and the cyber- and biology-unlocked twin, Mythos 5.2, stays limited to vetted organizations.

items.headline: Meta's new Muse Ember is a tiny, very cheap model built for the busywork agents repeat all day
items.explainer: At $0.10 in / $0.50 out per million tokens, Ember is meant for tool calls, quick coding fixes, sorting and reading long documents, and Meta says it matches Claude Haiku 5.5 at about a third of the cost per task. It's on the Meta Model API and Muse Code now, with a 1M-token context window, so cheap helper bots can run far more steps for pennies.

items.headline: ChatGPT dots can now use more than one of your computers and you pick which one per task
items.explainer: Connect each computer from the ChatGPT desktop app on it, then tell your dot which machine a task should run on, for example building and testing on a spare desktop while you keep working on your laptop. Each computer needs the ChatGPT app open and online, and you can revoke access per machine.

items.headline: ByteDance's Seedream 5.5 image model can keep editing one picture for 100 rounds without it degrading
items.explainer: Areas you didn't ask to change stay put, it can make images with transparent backgrounds ready to drop into a design, and photos and small text look more realistic. It's rolling out in Dreamina, CapCut and BytePlus.

items.headline: Your ChatGPT dot can now read sign-in codes from your inbox and log in for you
items.explainer: When a website emails a one-time sign-in code, your dot (ChatGPT's always-on agent) can now pull it from your connected inbox and finish the login, and you choose whether it may do that once or every time. Only allow it for accounts you're happy for the agent to enter, and still check that the task it logged in for actually got done.

items.headline: Meta's Muse can now build you a custom 'space' like a planner, tracker or game
items.explainer: Describe what you want (a gift tracker, wedding planner, school-events dashboard or trip planner) and Muse builds it as a space inside the app that you can pin to your tabs and keep editing. If you connect apps like Gmail, Calendar or OpenTable, a space updates itself in the background; it's available everywhere Muse is.

items.headline: Anthropic explains how 'dreaming' helps Claude fix and organize its memory between sessions
items.explainer: Anthropic shows how Claude can go back over its own past work while idle to correct wrong notes, merge duplicates and build a wiki of what it knows, so a long-running agent repeats fewer mistakes. It's an engineering explainer, not a new button, but it's a good model for any bot you run: have it review and tidy its notes regularly.

items.headline: Claude Code cloud sessions now set up your project on their own
items.explainer: On Pro, Max and Ultra plans, Claude works out which packages, network access and API keys a project needs in a cloud session and saves that setup for next time. Keys are stored as secrets that Claude never sees, so you no longer have to write a setup script before a cloud coding agent can start.

items.headline: ChatGPT Remix lets work teams copy a teammate's Site and make their own version
items.explainer: In ChatGPT Business and Enterprise, you can now take a Site a colleague built, tell ChatGPT what to change, and keep editing your own copy while the original stays untouched. It's rolling out to work accounts only, not personal plans.

items.headline: OpenCode Browse lets AI agents use your real browser, logins included
items.explainer: A free Chrome extension plus MCP server lets agents like OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor or Codex open background tabs in your own browser and use the sites you're already signed into. It hands the tab back to you for logins, 2FA and payments, and you can limit a session to sites you name; that's worth doing, because it acts as you.

items.headline: Meta brings Muse Wonder-style memory and focus to Muse and Meta AI
items.explainer: Muse and Meta AI get specialized models trained with Muse Wonder so they remember what still matters across chats (Active Memory) and keep pushing when a task hits a snag (Active Focus). Meta says Muse forgets critical goal details 2.4x less often and finishes everyday tasks with surprises 67% more often; Meta AI should ask sharper follow-ups and handle mid-chat course changes better.

items.headline: Amazon's Alexa for Shopping can now take shopping requests over text message
items.explainer: Invited U.S. customers can text Alexa Shopping to search, compare, build a cart, buy, track prices, and check orders—the same agent that already lives in the Amazon app and site. It's invite-only at first with a waitlist for others; confirm what it buys and what payment method it uses before you approve.

items.headline: Google Antigravity remote agents keep coding in the cloud when you close your laptop
items.explainer: On Google AI Pro and Ultra (personal accounts), Antigravity can run a coding session in a Google-managed cloud VM so work continues while you step away, and you can unblock permissions from your phone. Voice mode (Gemini Live) also rolls out for talking to the agent out loud, but voice does not work inside remote/cloud sessions yet.

items.headline: OpenAI partners with Hacktron to probe its own systems with AI security agents
items.explainer: OpenAI is bringing Hacktron's researchers in to hunt bugs in how OpenAI systems talk to third-party services, with expanded Daybreak Red model access. It's a security partnership for OpenAI's own defenses, not a new ChatGPT feature for everyday users.

items.headline: Baidu posts free download of its ERNIE 5.5 Flash base model for developers to train
items.explainer: Baidu released the raw (not chat-tuned) weights of ERNIE 5.5 Flash, a 280-billion-parameter model with only 14 billion active at a time, so developers can fine-tune their own assistants on it. It's a building block rather than an app you can chat with, and its license excludes the EU, UK and South Korea.

items.headline: Visa's shopping-agent test: AI buyers passed only about 57% of realistic runs
items.explainer: Visa put 22 models through 15 shopping chats where the customer leaves needs half-said; overall pass rate was 57.2%, and about half of the failures still ended in a purchase. Treat agent shopping as a helper that needs your confirmation—don't let it buy without a human check.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, a security model that finds and helps fix software bugs
items.explainer: Approved security teams can use GPT-6 Cyber to hunt for real software holes, check they work, and draft fixes, with stronger rules to stay inside the job they were given. It's only for Daybreak Red customers for now (not everyday ChatGPT), and OpenAI says it already helped find hundreds of Linux and Firefox issues.

items.headline: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes 15-second AI videos and cuts the price 30%
items.explainer: Ask Gemini to make a short video up to 15 seconds (was 10), then tweak it in chat—swap the background or lighting—without starting over. On the API it's $0.07 per second at 720p (30% cheaper than 1.1), and Ultra subscribers get 15-second clips in the Gemini app.

items.headline: Claude can now read your bank and card accounts and answer money questions (US beta)
items.explainer: On Pro, Max and Ultra in the US, connect selected bank, card, loan or investment accounts through Plaid and ask Claude where your money went, what's due before payday, or whether a trip fits the budget. Access is read-only so Claude can't move or invest money, chats in the Personal Finance hub aren't used for training, and Anthropic says it isn't designed to give investment advice.

items.headline: Muse gets real-time voice chat and expressive avatars in the US
items.explainer: In the Muse app on mobile, web and Mac in the US, tap the phone icon to talk out loud while your Muse's avatar reacts with expressions and gestures, and pick from hundreds of voices. Meta says it's useful for thinking through a trip or rehearsing an interview hands-free, with AI Glasses and Muse Charm support coming later.

items.headline: Perplexity launches Teammates, always-on work agents for Max subscribers
items.explainer: On the web for Max subscribers, Teammates take ongoing jobs using your Computer projects, skills, memory and tools, can work with other teammates and message coworkers in Slack, and you can review or redirect what they do. Native mobile and desktop apps are coming later; Verge notes it needs the $200/month Max plan.

items.headline: Cursor's cloud agent can build a web app, set up a database and publish a shareable link
items.explainer: On paid plans with cloud agents on, ask a cloud agent to build an app and Cursor can scaffold it, provision Postgres and auth behind Cursor SSO, run security checks, then deploy only after you approve publish. Team admins can see every app and secret, and individual plans can share apps publicly.

items.headline: Mistral Studio adds managed agents, apps and stronger workflows for enterprise bots
items.explainer: Developers can write an agent once in Python and run it locally, self-hosted or Mistral-managed, with durable background runs, approval gates and Studio tracing. Apps and Managed Agents are in public preview; Mistral also shipped a natural-language workflow builder and HTTP API connectors the same day.

items.headline: Thinking Machines Lab launches Inkling 2 Small, with open weights planned soon
items.explainer: A 594B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (about 17B active) for coding, vision and long autonomous work is available on Tinker for inference and fine-tuning today. Full weights are planned under Apache 2.0 after more safety testing, so self-hosted bots may get a strong new option next week.

items.headline: OpenAI's AI agents found and drafted patches for 948 Linux 'get root' security holes
items.explainer: In one mid-October test, OpenAI's autonomous security pipeline checked the Linux kernel, proved 948 ways a normal user could become admin, and wrote candidate patches for human review, at about $1.2 million in API cost. Humans still review and report the fixes; the run used an upcoming cyber model that became GPT-6 Cyber.

items.headline: Meta buys Conductor, the app that runs several coding agents on one project at once
items.explainer: Conductor's founder says the team is joining Meta to build a new coding interface with Meta's AI labs. The cloud service shuts down November 20 (local app keeps working into early 2027), so export any cloud projects before then.

items.headline: OpenAI will buy Pierre to give Codex better Git storage and code-review tools
items.explainer: Pierre already powers file browsing and diffs inside Codex; OpenAI wants its Code Storage service too so coding agents can keep and review code like a normal Git workflow. Open-source Pierre tools stay open; the deal still needs regulatory approval.

items.headline: ChatGPT Images 2.6 can make animated GIFs and remember a saved reference photo
items.explainer: Ask ChatGPT for a looping GIF or to animate a still photo, and save a photo (say, of your dog) under a name so you can reuse it later by typing @ and that name. It's on all ChatGPT plans and in Codex, about 50% faster than before, with GIFs rolling out gradually; ChatGPT can't edit an animated GIF you upload.

items.headline: Grok Bot can now phone businesses for you, like cancelling a plan or booking an appointment
items.explainer: Tell Grok Bot who to call and why, approve the call, and it waits on hold, works the phone menu and talks to the agent while you watch a live transcript and can take over at any time, then it sends you a summary. It only calls U.S. numbers for now (not Washington or Illinois), says up front that it's a virtual assistant, and some reps may refuse to deal with an AI.

items.headline: Ricursive releases Ripple-65B Preview, a free open coding model small enough to run on a high-end laptop
items.explainer: Ripple-65B is a downloadable model (Apache 2.0 license) that its maker says is the best U.S. open model at agent-style coding, and it can run on a MacBook Pro or NVIDIA DGX Spark. Hosted versions start around $0.20 in / $0.60 out per million tokens on OpenRouter; the benchmark scores are Ricursive's own.

items.headline: Anthropic's lab used Claude to map a mystery protein 'vault' from bacteria-infecting viruses
items.explainer: Claude searched billions of proteins, designed the DNA and processed the microscope data, so a step that normally takes three days took about 90 minutes and a first 3D model was ready in 34 hours. It's an example of AI speeding up real lab science; the scientists still chose what to test, and the paper isn't peer-reviewed yet.

items.headline: Tencent releases Hy4, an open-weight model that can now see images and run longer agent tasks
items.explainer: Hy4 is one of the strongest open models you can get, now with image and chart understanding and better long multi-step tasks, at about $0.90 per million input tokens and $2.70 per million output tokens (half off on Tencent Cloud through Dec 31). Tencent says the downloadable weights come in the next few days and admits it still trails the top closed models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

items.headline: Netflix tests an AI Discover tab that picks something to watch based on your mood
items.explainer: Pick a theme like "something light", "scare me" or "quick watches" and Netflix's AI suggests titles, and you can tell it to stop showing ones you don't want. It's rolling out first to English-language US members on supported TVs, as an experiment Netflix may change.

items.headline: Google brings Guided Learning homework help to Classroom and Search, and switches Gemini off by default for K-12 students
items.explainer: Guided Learning walks a student through a problem step by step instead of handing over the answer; it's live worldwide in Google Classroom for teacher-assigned work and is being piloted in Search at select US schools this month. Parents should know that Gemini and Search will be off by default for K-12 school accounts until the school turns them on, and Search can't be enabled without its AI features.

items.headline: OpenAI shows ChatGPT and Codex designing physical products, including a small device built with almost no human edits
items.explainer: OpenAI says its models now help engineers with CAD drawings, circuit boards and simulations, and two staff used GPT-6 Astra to design a small Codex talk-to device that a factory then built in under a month. It's a progress report and a call for engineering partners, not a new product you can buy, and OpenAI admits the model still missed manufacturing limits that humans had to fix.

items.headline: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve, a way to mathematically prove which AI model wrote a reply
items.explainer: FlashProve lets an AI company publish a fingerprint of its model and then attach a proof to each answer showing that exact model produced it, so you could check you're not being quietly served a cheaper model. It's an early research prototype (tested on Meta's open Llama 4 Maverick, short 1,024-token requests only), and Anthropic hasn't said it will offer proofs for Claude.

items.headline: Google's Dreambeans app, which turns your Gmail, Photos and Calendar into illustrated daily stories, launches in India
items.explainer: If you're in India and 18+, you can now try Google's experimental Dreambeans app in English and 13 Indian languages; it reads only the Google apps you connect (Gmail, Photos, Calendar, Search, Gemini, YouTube) to make a personal daily story feed. It's its first country outside the US, it can get things wrong, and you can disconnect apps or delete your data in the app.

items.headline: xAI shows Data Bot, a shared Grok Bot that answers any employee's data questions like a data scientist
items.explainer: xAI's data team taught a shared Team Bot their metrics, experiment rules and chart styles, so anyone can ask it in chat or Slack to dig into numbers or build a dashboard. xAI estimates it did about 70 hours of the data team's work in one week (its own figure), and it's a how-we-use-it example you can copy with Team Bots, not a separate product.

items.headline: Google retires Gemini 2.5 Pro and 2.5 Flash in its API; from Dec 1 requests are switched to newer models and billed at their rates
items.explainer: If a bot or app you use still calls Gemini 2.5 Pro or 2.5 Flash, it will quietly be moved on Dec 1, 2026: 2.5 Pro goes to Gemini 3.8 Flash and 2.5 Flash to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, billed at those models' prices. Some features work differently on the new models, so whoever runs the bot should switch and test before then.

items.headline: Apple Watch's AI that rewinds the last 15 seconds of a conversation and writes recaps of your day enters beta
items.explainer: On Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, Live Rewind shows the last 15 seconds of what someone said as text when you double-press the crown, and Siri Recap can take short summary notes of conversations (on a schedule you set) that delete after 7 days unless saved. It's a developer beta in English for now; Apple says no audio is recorded, but the people you talk to haven't opted in, so tell them.

items.headline: Claude's API can now remember the conversation for you, making long agent sessions about a third faster to answer
items.explainer: If you use Claude-powered agents or coding tools, long sessions should start replying faster: with the new message threads beta the server keeps the conversation, so the app only sends new messages, and Anthropic says the median wait for the first word drops about 35% on very long (500k to 1M token) chats. Price and token use stay the same, and a thread expires five minutes after its last request.

items.headline: OpenAI releases LifeVal, a test of how well AI handles everyday life chores like childcare, groceries and government forms
items.explainer: It's a sign of where ChatGPT is headed: OpenAI built the test from time-use surveys and a survey of 3,995 people about the tasks they most want help with, such as budgeting, ordering groceries or finding a home, and frames it as a step toward ChatGPT acting as a personal assistant. Its own showcase tasks score 90 to 100%, but it's OpenAI grading its own homework, so treat it as a direction, not proof.

items.headline: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, a giant agent model that plugs into Claude Code and Codex
items.explainer: Food-delivery giant Meituan's new model (1.6 trillion parameters, about 48 billion active at a time) sees images, reads up to 1 million tokens and is built for long coding and agent jobs; it works inside the Claude Code, Codex and Hermes tools. It's API-only for now through the LongCat platform and was trained on Chinese-made chips, so it's mainly for developers shopping for cheaper agent models.

items.headline: New GDPx test finds even the best AI agent finishes only 12% of real expert work tasks
items.explainer: A useful reality check before handing an agent serious professional work: across 206 long tasks in 11 fields, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 12.0%, Gemini 4 Carbon 10.9% and GPT-6 Astra 9.6%, and every model scored zero on the finance and legal tasks under pass/fail grading. SemiAnalysis says it will refresh the leaderboard every three to six months.

items.headline: ChatGPT will merge its Chat and Work tabs into one, and the old ChatGPT Classic desktop app retires Jan 30, 2027
items.explainer: Soon you won't have to pick between Chat and Work: a small test group gets one screen where you can talk, bring in files and plugins, and have ChatGPT build a site, make slides or act on the web, while Codex stays separate. If you still use the ChatGPT Classic Mac app, move to the new ChatGPT desktop app before Jan 30, 2027; your chat history comes with you.

more_sources.label: OpenAI Help Center: new desktop app

items.headline: Claude adds an invisible text watermark to more models, including Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6, from Nov 3
items.explainer: Text from Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 will carry a hidden mark that lets Anthropic later recognize it as AI-written, which it says is for the EU AI Act; it doesn't change how replies look and contains no personal info. Amazon Bedrock follows a few days later, and the detection tool is only in private preview.

items.headline: ChatGPT and Codex will share one usage allowance from December, and paid accounts per device are now capped
items.explainer: On Plus, Pro and Business, your chats and your Codex or agent work will draw from one token-based pool, so long agent jobs can eat into your chat time (Instant chats don't count). Check Settings > Usage to see your balance; OpenAI also now limits how many paid ChatGPT accounts one device or card can hold, so juggling several cheap subscriptions may stop working.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Super-agent, an always-on coding agent that takes requests from team chat
items.explainer: It watches one GitHub repo (and optionally a Feishu chat), picks up requests from people you allow, works on them in parallel and comes back with a pull request, pinging you only when needed. It's a free MIT-licensed research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product, so it's for tinkerers who can run it themselves.

items.headline: Apple Intelligence comes to iPhones in China with iOS 27.3, with Alibaba's Qwen built in
items.explainer: iPhone owners in China get Writing Tools, Live Translation, Visual Intelligence, Clean Up, Genmoji and summaries, with Qwen answering inside Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, much like ChatGPT does elsewhere. Testing starts in the iOS 27.3 beta on Nov 4 with the full release in December; the new Siri isn't included.

items.headline: Text from Grok's API will carry an invisible watermark by default from Nov 7
items.explainer: Apps and bots built on Grok 4.x through the API will produce text that xAI can later recognize as AI-written, which it says is for the EU AI Act; nothing changes in how the text looks. Team admins can opt out per model, and the Grok app itself isn't covered by this change.

items.headline: Claude renames Max 20x to Ultra and drops the five-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts
items.explainer: At the same $200 a month, verified Ultra subscribers can now use their whole week's allowance whenever they like instead of hitting a reset every five hours; the weekly limit itself didn't change. The $100 Max 5x plan is now just called Max, and you don't need to do anything if you subscribe.

items.headline: ChatGPT's phone apps let you stay signed in to two accounts and switch between them
items.explainer: Handy if you have a personal and a work ChatGPT: switch in a tap instead of logging out. Each account keeps its own chats, memory, files and subscription, and it's rolling out gradually on iOS and Android.

items.headline: ChatGPT tightens weapons answers for teens and can end chats fixated on violence
items.explainer: If a teen in your house uses ChatGPT, it will now refuse more weapons details, and for everyone it limits step-by-step recreations of past mass attacks. It can also end conversations stuck on violence and may briefly pause an account, and OpenAI says it will publish its first community safety report in early 2027.

items.headline: Zest launches a restaurant agent you just text, and it books tables for your group chat
items.explainer: Text it what you're craving and it suggests places and books through OpenTable, Resy or SevenRooms, with no app to install. Add it to a group chat and it runs a vote on where to eat; linking a credit card lets it learn where you actually like to eat, so only share that if you're comfortable.

items.headline: Reality check: DoorDash has seen only 'several hundred' orders from outside AI shopping agents
items.explainer: Agents like Meta's Muse can order food for you, but almost nobody is doing it yet: DoorDash counts a few hundred agent orders against millions of normal ones, and Amazon's CEO called outside shopping agents 'still not great.' For now, your bot works best for finding and comparing; expect to finish checkout yourself on many stores.

items.headline: Gemini's Computer Use tool is now generally available for developers
items.explainer: Apps built on Gemini can now officially let the AI look at a screen and click, type and scroll in a browser, desktop or phone. Expect more third-party bots that fill in forms for you, and look for ones that ask before checking out or changing sensitive info, which Google turns on by default.

items.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back one shared robots.txt switch to keep a website out of AI training
items.explainer: If you run a blog or small business site, you'll soon be able to say 'don't train AI on this' once, for every participating AI company, instead of blocking each crawler separately. Anthropic already honors it, OpenAI says support comes in the next few months, and Google and Microsoft (from Feb 1, 2027) follow next year; it's based on an IETF draft that isn't final yet.

items.headline: Pika releases H3 Flex, a fast video-with-sound model with open weights
items.explainer: It makes a 15-second clip with a soundtrack in seconds, can follow up to 12 reference images, videos or voice clips, and upscales your favorite to 4K. It's on the Pika API now and comes to the Pika app on Nov 2; the downloadable weights' license excludes the US, EU, UK and Korea.

items.headline: ElevenLabs launches SFX v3, which turns one sentence into a layered sound scene
items.explainer: Describe a scene, like rain, thunder and a dog barking, and it now gets each sound in, in order, with cleaner audio and better music and vocals. Handy for giving home videos, reels or school projects real sound; it's in the ElevenLabs app, ElevenCreative and the API.

items.headline: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro's Work and Codex limits and cancels the planned Pro 200 cut
items.explainer: Same price, more agent time: Pro 100 and Pro 500 now get twice their previous Work and Codex allowance, Business Premium gets more too, and the Pro 200 reduction announced in September is off. It applies automatically from Oct 29, and usage by your dot still counts separately.

items.headline: Google is shutting down Jules, its background coding agent, and folding it into Antigravity
items.explainer: If you used Jules to fix bugs or write code in the background, start moving that work to Google's Antigravity, which will get Jules-style remote tasks. Google hasn't given a shutdown date yet, so save anything you need from Jules now.

items.headline: Meta quietly launches Style Sketch, an AI app that plans outfits from the clothes you own
items.explainer: It builds a virtual closet from your Instagram photos or pictures you snap, suggests outfits, shows them on a model matched to your body, and plans day-by-day trip outfits using the weather. For now it's only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.

items.headline: Mistral releases the weights of Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'), now the strongest open model for coding
items.explainer: Anyone can now download Mistral's biggest model and run it on their own servers, so private, self-hosted bots get a lot more capable. Mistral says it's the best open-weight model for coding and defensive security; on its API it now costs $0.70 in / $2.10 out per million tokens, and it's also on OpenRouter and Microsoft Foundry.

items.headline: Claude's phone apps add CarPlay voice chats, account switching and a faster voice mode
items.explainer: You can now talk to Claude hands-free through Apple CarPlay (open it from the car screen first) and stay signed in to a personal and a work account at once. Voice mode answers faster, copes better with noisy rooms and now speaks 33 languages; on iPad, what Claude makes opens beside the chat.

items.headline: Gemini can now make and edit documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets right in the chat
items.explainer: Ask Gemini for a file, like a PDF study guide from photos of your handwritten notes, then type your own edits or highlight a part and ask Gemini to change it. It's free for all users; PDFs work on web and mobile, other formats on the web only.

items.headline: Alexa for Shopping can now handle 100+ Amazon chores, from skipping deliveries to tracking refunds
items.explainer: In the Amazon app or website you can just ask Alexa to edit lists and registries, skip or pause Subscribe & Save, change delivery instructions, check Prime benefits or chase a refund. It's live for all US Amazon customers; check what it changed on your account, especially billing.

items.headline: OpenAI rewrites its rulebook for how ChatGPT should behave around five core values
items.explainer: OpenAI's updated Model Spec tells its models to follow what you actually mean, avoid harm, be honest about what they did and don't know, respect your choices and show care. It also adds guidance for agents acting on your behalf and changes some default behaviors, so ChatGPT may answer a bit differently over time.

items.headline: Granola, the meeting-notes app, now types for you by voice in any app, free
items.explainer: On a Mac, hold the Fn key and talk; Granola cleans up your words and types them into email, chats or AI prompts, with unlimited words for free. iOS and Windows are coming soon.

items.headline: Gemini lets you share your avatar so friends can put you in AI images and videos
items.explainer: Create an avatar of yourself in Gemini, share it with a friend's Gmail address, and they can tag you with @ in prompts to make pictures and videos of you together. You choose who can use it and can take access away at any time.

items.headline: Shopify lets AI agents shop for you across a billion products and pay with Shop Pay
items.explainer: You can now point ChatGPT, Claude or another assistant at Shopify's shop.md skill and have it search over a billion products, check out with Shop Pay and track your orders, and Shop Pay also works inside Meta's Muse, Claude Duet, Grok Bot and Instinct. Your card is never shared with the bot and you still approve each purchase, but double-check what's in the cart before you say yes.

items.headline: ChatGPT Pro and Business plans now come with up to $500 a month of free API credits
items.explainer: If you pay for ChatGPT Pro you get API credits equal to your plan price ($100, $200 or $500 a month), and Business workspaces get $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat, capped at $500, so running your own bots on OpenAI's API can cost nothing extra. Credits expire each billing cycle, need a paid plan at least 7 days old and the same email on both accounts, and don't cover Codex or Plus.

items.headline: Grok's API now takes plain-language guidelines for how to handle sensitive topics
items.explainer: Developers can add a guidelines field to Grok API requests to steer how it handles specific content categories, which makes Grok-powered bots easier to keep on-brand and family-safe. It's available to all API customers; nothing changes in the Grok app itself.

items.headline: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its new top model, but only a few security teams can use it so far
items.explainer: Carbon is Google's strongest model yet: it now ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is built for long coding jobs and for finding and fixing security holes. This week only selected cyber defenders get it; Google says developers, businesses and the Gemini app get it 'as soon as possible', at the same intro API price as Argon ($2 in / $10 out per million tokens, later $4 / $20).

items.headline: You can now text your ChatGPT dot over iMessage or RCS
items.explainer: Your dot (ChatGPT's always-on agent) can now take tasks by text, photo or voice note from your phone's Messages app, and text you back when something needs you. It's a beta for US ChatGPT Pro users only, one-to-one (no group chats), and it can't see your other text conversations.

items.headline: Claude for Legal gets ready-made tools for contract review, cite checks and rule tracking
items.explainer: Legal teams can start from a gallery of ready-to-use Claude 'artifacts', such as a contract comparison table, a citation checker and a regulation timeline, add their own documents and share them with coworkers. Every answer links back to its source, and a lawyer still reviews the result; it's aimed at businesses and law firms, not personal legal advice.

items.headline: Google opens Gemini and Search to more outside apps, starting with Adobe, Calm and Peloton
items.explainer: More of the apps you already use will work right inside the Gemini app and Google Search, so you can ask Gemini to plan a Peloton workout or use Adobe without switching apps. Google launched a developer preview (US, waitlist) that lets any app plug in through MCP; more than 50 Connected Apps are live, and Calm is coming to both Search and Gemini.

items.headline: GitHub Copilot Fusion picks the AI model for you, and Microsoft opens its Copilot agent engine to builders
items.explainer: If you code with GitHub Copilot, you can now choose 'Copilot Fusion' and an effort level instead of a model; it routes each task to cheaper or stronger models and GitHub says it came within 2 points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 at about half the cost per task (30% off for paid plans through Nov 30). Microsoft also made the harness behind Copilot available in Microsoft Foundry, so companies can build their own agents on it.

items.headline: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free open model that writes up recordings and says who spoke
items.explainer: Expect better, cheaper meeting-notes and transcription bots: this free, open-weight model transcribes 40 languages, translates, tells up to eight speakers apart and handles recordings up to an hour. It works on recorded audio, not live calls, and is meant for app builders rather than a ready-made app.

items.headline: Perplexity's voice mode can now run several Computer tasks at once
items.explainer: On the Mac app and web, Pro and Max subscribers can talk to Perplexity to start new Computer tasks, check on several running at once and manage Projects in one voice session. It now runs on OpenAI's gpt-live-1 voice model, which can listen while it talks.

items.headline: Gemini adds interactive 'immersive explorations' for learning a topic layer by layer
items.explainer: Students and curious adults can zoom through interactive scenes, like inside a jet engine or along the Silk Road, and tap labels to dig deeper. It's free for all users from the Gemini student hub for now, with direct access in chats and audio narration coming soon.

items.headline: Meta tests Waddle World, an AI virtual pet app, in the Philippines
items.explainer: Waddle World is a Tamagotchi-style app where an AI pixel pet gets to know you, turns what you tell it into illustrated journal entries and can send a weekly email. It's a test in the Philippines only (iOS and Android, 18+), and Meta says it's not a chatbot or an assistant.

items.headline: Grok Bot can now buy things you approve, track the order and cancel subscriptions you don't use
items.explainer: Grok Bot 0.78.1 shows shopping results as product cards with a Buy now button that still waits for your OK, then tracks the package. New templates start a free trial and cancel it before it bills, find unused subscriptions and watch renewal prices, and the Bot confirms with you before changing anything.

items.headline: Google DeepMind shows Genie 4, a world model you can steer like a live video game
items.explainer: Genie 4 builds a realistic, explorable scene from a text prompt, with sound and talking characters, and changes it in real time when you type things like 'make it rain'. It's only with trusted testers for now; Google says Google AI Ultra subscribers (in Project Genie) and early Gemini API partners come next, so there's nothing for your bots to use yet.

items.headline: Liquid AI releases LFM3, free small models that run on a phone or laptop
items.explainer: LFM3 is a family of six open-weight 2B-size models for text, images, audio and more; the text one fits in about 1 GB and reads up to 256K tokens. That makes it a good fit for a private bot that runs on your own device, and anyone handy can fine-tune it on a single GPU.

items.headline: Microsoft's MAI Image 2.7 photo editor ranks near the top, in preview
items.explainer: Microsoft's new image-editing model can relight a scene, change text on a sign, or restore an old photo while keeping it looking natural. It's in preview in MAI Playground and debuts #3 on Arena's image-edit leaderboard, so expect sharper edit-my-photo features in Microsoft apps.

items.headline: Apple puts an AI assistant in Pages, Keynote and Numbers, and opens them to outside agents
items.explainer: Your bot will be able to read and edit Pages, Keynote and Numbers files on a Mac. Apple's new assistant (built on Apple models and OpenAI) drafts text, builds slides and charts data, and new MCP support lets outside AI agents work in the apps directly; it arrives in November for Apple Creator Studio subscribers ($12.99/month), in beta, US English only, and MCP needs macOS 27.

items.headline: Meta's Muse personal agent launches in Singapore, its first country after the US
items.explainer: Muse, Meta's do-it-for-you agent, now works in Singapore with local apps like Grab, Shopee and Singapore Airlines. It's free for most tasks, keeps your passwords and cards out of the agent's view, and asks before sending an email or buying anything.

items.headline: OpenAI and Oracle plan to bring Oracle business apps into ChatGPT
items.explainer: If your job runs on Oracle software, you may soon handle approved tasks like finance or HR lookups by asking ChatGPT. Oracle AI Workspace is still in development with no launch date; what's live now is that US Oracle customers can buy ChatGPT Work, Codex and the OpenAI API through Oracle Marketplace.

items.headline: Anthropic gives US federal, state and local governments 40% off Claude
items.explainer: Government offices can now buy Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the Claude API at 40% off with no minimum spend. Prices for everyone else don't change, but your city or state may start using Claude for forms and backlogs.

items.headline: Gemini API now saves requests by default for new paid projects
items.explainer: If you set up a new paid Gemini API project, the prompts your bot sends are now stored by default, matching Google's Interactions API; existing projects don't change. If you'd rather they weren't kept, send store=false or turn off Generate Content API logging under Logs and Datasets.

items.headline: GPT-6.1 Terra: OpenAI's new fast, cheaper model for bots that use apps and screens
items.explainer: GPT-6.1 Terra is a new mid-size OpenAI model that's better at reading what's on a screen and clicking through apps for you, like filling out forms or entering invoices, and makes fewer factual mistakes than GPT-5.6 Terra. It's in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API at $1 in / $5 out per million tokens, half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol, so bots that do lots of computer work get cheaper to run; the benchmark claims are OpenAI's own.

more_sources.label: AWS: GPT-6.1 Terra on Amazon Bedrock

items.headline: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, files to go public on Nasdaq
items.explainer: Anthropic has filed the paperwork with the SEC for a stock market listing under the symbol ANT; the share count and price aren't set yet. Nothing changes in Claude for you today, but a public Anthropic will have to report its business openly, which can shape pricing and plans down the road.

items.headline: Claude gets a free plugin for nonprofits that helps with fundraising, marketing and hiring
items.explainer: Verified nonprofits using Claude now get a plugin, built with about 30 nonprofits, with ready-made skills for grant research, donor reports, marketing and hiring that follow the group's own policies. If you volunteer for or run a small nonprofit, it's a quicker way to get Claude doing the paperwork that eats your week.

items.headline: Riverside adds a team of AI agents that edit, clip and post your videos and podcasts
items.explainer: If you record a podcast or videos on Riverside, four new agents can now prep your interview questions, edit the recording into a finished episode, cut social clips, and write captions and schedule posts. They're on web and mobile on every Riverside plan (some features depend on your tier), and nothing goes live until you approve it.

more_sources.label: Forbes: Riverside Agents are a new team for AI production of podcasts

items.headline: Ant Group's LingGuang 2.0 turns its AI assistant into a helper that acts before you ask
items.explainer: Ant Group, the company behind Alipay, upgraded its LingGuang app into a personal agent that, with your permission, keeps working after you close the chat, following up on tasks and flagging things like price drops on a trip you booked or a subscription you forgot. It's another sign that everyday assistants are moving from answering questions to quietly running errands in the background.

items.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro: a new open model that says it nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 at coding
items.explainer: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro is in the Kimi apps and API, and its full weights are now on Hugging Face (under Moonshot's own Kimi K3.1 Pro License), though at 2.8 trillion parameters it needs data-center hardware to run. Its API price is $2 in / $10 out per million tokens, half of Claude Opus 5.5's list price; the coding scores are Moonshot's own.

items.headline: Cursor's coding bot can now click and type in other apps on your computer
items.explainer: After you update the Cursor app, its agent can drive desktop apps such as the iPhone simulator to test the features it just built, instead of you tapping through them yourself. Because it works by looking at your screen, close private windows before you let it take over.

items.headline: NVIDIA releases a free 4GB AI model for assistants that run on your own device
items.explainer: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is a small, free open model built for fast local voice and device assistants that can follow instructions and use tools, so a simple bot can run on your own computer with no per-message bill. It's text-only with a 64K-token memory, so save bigger jobs for the large cloud models.

items.headline: Block shows Dessa, a voice AI that talks with human-like pauses and emotion
items.explainer: Dessa is a speech model from the company behind Square and Cash App that listens and talks at the same time, so conversations with it sound strikingly like a real person. There's no public access yet, only early access for safety researchers, but it's a reminder that a lifelike voice on the phone may not be a person.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts its newest models off the live internet while they're being trained
items.explainer: OpenAI says its frontier models now train in an offline copy of the web instead of the real internet, a safety step so a model in training can't reach outside systems. Nothing changes in ChatGPT for you, but it shows labs are treating stronger models as something to keep fenced in.

items.headline: OpenAI's Agents API can now run bots on a schedule
items.explainer: Developers can now tell an OpenAI agent to run on a repeating schedule, like every morning at 10, or once at a set time, and the agent can even set up its own schedules when you ask in plain words. Expect more apps that do a recurring job for you, such as a daily digest, without you opening them.

items.headline: OpenAI switched off older models including GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, o4-mini and gpt-image-1
items.explainer: If an older app or bot of yours suddenly stopped working on Oct 23, this may be why: OpenAI retired a batch of older models announced back in April. Switching it to a current model such as GPT-5.6 usually fixes it.

items.headline: Claude Enterprise merges chat and Cowork into one Claude that keeps working in the cloud
items.explainer: At companies on Claude Enterprise, people no longer pick between a quick chat and handing Claude a bigger job: every conversation starts as a chat and moves into the cloud when it needs to work with files or code, then hands back the finished document or deck. The work keeps going after you close your laptop, and admins get controls and a new Efficient mode to manage usage.

items.headline: Gemini can now create notebooks and add sources to Gemini Notebook from your chat
items.explainer: Type @Gemini Notebook in a Gemini chat to make a notebook, add a link or this chat as a source, or ask what your notebooks say, without switching apps. It's on by default for personal and Workspace accounts outside Europe, so double-check before asking it to delete anything, since it can change your notebooks too.

more_sources.label: 9to5Google: Gemini Notebook now a Connected App

items.headline: Anthropic hands Agent Skills to a neutral foundation
items.explainer: Skills are little instruction folders that teach an AI agent a specific task, and more than 70 tools, including ChatGPT, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, already read them. Moving the standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation makes it more likely a skill you set up once keeps working across different bots.

items.headline: OpenAI's quick-answer Decisions API is now open to all developers
items.explainer: The Decisions API turns text or images into short typed answers, like sorting an email or approving a request, without writing a full reply, and it now handles up to 400 questions per request with prompt-cache discounts. Apps built on it can make these small calls faster and cheaper, which adds up for bots that triage a lot.

items.headline: Canva launches Craft, its own image model built for designs with readable text
items.explainer: Craft plans the layout first, then makes images up to 2K in about 30 sizes, and is trained on human-made Canva templates so text comes out legible. It's available to all Canva users in the Dream Lab tab, and Canva plans to let ChatGPT and Gemini use it too.

items.headline: Claude will stop asking permission for every step, starting next week
items.explainer: Starting next week, Claude's web, desktop and mobile apps on Pro, Max and Team plans begin sessions in auto mode, where an automated check lets safe actions go ahead and blocks risky ones instead of asking you to approve each step. Longer tasks finish with fewer interruptions, and you can switch any session back to manual approvals.

items.headline: Grok Bot can now use your phone's Calendar, Reminders and Contacts
items.explainer: With your permission, Grok Bot on iOS and Android can add calendar events, set and check reminders, look up contacts and reach apps like Messages and Home, and you allow each app separately. That makes "add this to my calendar" or "remind me tonight" something you can just ask your bot to do; it's rolling out now.

items.headline: Grok Bot can sign in to your accounts with 1Password, without seeing your passwords
items.explainer: You approve which saved logins your bot may use, and 1Password fills them in, one-time codes included, so the bot never sees the password. 1Password says the same approach is rolling out for Meta's Muse and coming soon to Claude Duet and ChatGPT Work, at no extra cost on its Individual and Family plans.

items.headline: Gemini can now plan your day from your Google Maps saved places and calendar
items.explainer: If you turn on Personal Intelligence, Gemini can check your Maps searches and saved places alongside your Calendar, so "which restaurant on my list is near my last meeting?" gets a real answer. Google is also telling AI Ultra subscribers that Gemini 4 Argon will soon replace the Deep Think mode.

items.headline: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, a proactive agent that comes to you
items.explainer: Claude Duet sends you a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps an eye on them through the day, works on tasks while you're away, and asks before it does anything big like paying or deleting. It's a waitlist research preview for US Pro and Max subscribers, on iOS, Android and claude.ai, and Anthropic says it can still misjudge what's urgent.

items.headline: AI agents helped find critical PHP flaws that affect most websites
items.explainer: If you run a website or blog on PHP (WordPress included), make sure your host has updated PHP to the patched version now. OpenAI says its models helped researchers find the bugs before attackers did, and it's sharing a version checker and a Codex skill to help site owners check.

items.headline: Claude Security now re-scans your code every time it changes
items.explainer: Teams on Claude Enterprise can connect their code once and Claude keeps checking new changes for security holes, marking each one fixed when the fix lands. It's a public beta for businesses, not something personal plans get.

items.headline: OpenAI's models are coming to Google Cloud
items.explainer: Companies on Google Cloud will be able to use GPT-6 models and Codex without a separate OpenAI account (private preview now, wider launch planned in the coming weeks). For you it mostly means more places your work tools can quietly plug in OpenAI models.

items.headline: Recursive releases Flint, a free coding model that runs on a laptop
items.explainer: Flint is a free, open coding model small enough to run on an ordinary laptop, so a coding bot can work offline, keep your files private and skip per-use fees. Its maker says it still needs smaller, step-by-step tasks than the big paid assistants.

items.headline: Walmart opens its store to AI shopping agents, with spending limits you set
items.explainer: Walmart is building a direct connection so approved AI agents like ChatGPT, Gemini and Muse can search and buy from Walmart and Sam's Club for you, starting with an invite-only beta for developers. Next month, each agent gets its own profile in your Walmart account where you can require approval for every order or set a spending cap, and agents never see your card details.

more_sources.label: TechCrunch: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat
Retail Dive: Walmart welcomes external AI agents

items.headline: Mistral launches Voxtral 3 for voice agents that can take calls
items.explainer: A new set of speech models plus a kit for building phone and web voice agents that listen, look things up and talk back in 50+ languages. Mistral lists its voice agent API at $0.04 a minute with Mistral Small 4, so phone bots keep getting cheaper to run.

items.headline: OpenAI adds 12-hour prompt caching
items.explainer: Bots that run hours apart (like a morning and an evening check) can now keep their fixed instructions cached and pay the lower cached-input price. Writing to the 12-hour cache costs 2.5x the normal input price, so it pays off when the same setup is reused several times.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the engine that runs its own API
items.explainer: DeepInfer is the software DeepSeek uses to serve V4.1 Flash cheaply, now free under Apache 2.0. Hosting companies can copy the tricks, which could push the price of running open models down for your bots.

items.headline: Meta pauses Muse chat sharing after shared chats turned up on the web
items.explainer: Researchers found more than 6,800 Muse share links through public web records, some showing loan applications, revenue reviews and work calendars, so Meta switched sharing off while it reviews. Treat any AI "share link" as public, and keep private details out of chats you share.

items.headline: Gemini in your car can now use your Gmail, Calendar and Maps to help
items.explainer: With your permission, Gemini on Android Auto can pull your flight gate from email, find the restaurant you saved, or take you to your next appointment without you looking anything up. It's rolling out now on Android Auto for eligible personal accounts and is off until you turn it on.

items.headline: ChatGPT lets you lock private chats behind a PIN
items.explainer: You can now lock a sensitive ChatGPT chat from its ••• menu so it's hidden from your history and search and opens only with a 4-digit PIN or your phone's face or fingerprint unlock. Write the PIN down, because resetting a forgotten one deletes every locked chat for good; it's rolling out gradually.

more_sources.label: OpenAI Help Center: Using locked chats

items.headline: Google turns Gemini Gems into Skills and moves Spark into the main chat
items.explainer: From November 17, Google starts converting personal Gems into Skills you call with a slash in the main chat, and Scheduled Actions no longer need a paid plan (still rolling out to free accounts). If you built a Gem-based bot, test it before the switch.

items.headline: DeepSeek updates its V4.1 Flash model: faster and shorter answers, same price
items.explainer: DeepSeek says the update finishes tasks faster with shorter outputs, which means fewer tokens to pay for. The API name and prices are unchanged, and the open weights are on Hugging Face.

items.headline: DeepSeek opens its own web search and page-fetch tools to developers
items.explainer: Bots built on DeepSeek can now search the web and read pages through DeepSeek's own API at $0.75 per 1,000 requests each. Calls made through some coding agents are free until billing starts on November 1 (Beijing time).

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model so far
items.explainer: Meta's new open model is built for coding and agent work, and you can call it on day one through Groq, OpenRouter, Together AI and other APIs. Groq runs it at 350+ tokens per second per user. That speed matters for agents, because each task is a long chain of model calls.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok Voice 3.0, its new speech-to-speech model
items.explainer: The voice model behind Grok Bot's voice mode and Tesla's in-car assistant got an upgrade, at the same $0.08 a minute on the API. xAI says it answers in under a second and handles interruptions, which is what makes a phone bot feel natural.

items.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now available to developers and paid Gemini users
items.explainer: Google's new top model is in the API at an introductory $2 / $10 per million tokens, and in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google built it for long, multi-step work, the kind agents do.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model
items.explainer: Meta says Muse Wonder will soon power its Muse personal agent, starting with paying subscribers. Developers can use it through Meta's API at $4 / $20 per million tokens.

items.headline: Gemini's Spark agent moves to a "Task" button on the app's home screen
items.explainer: Handing a job to Google's background agent is now one tap away in the Gemini app, with a new Scheduled page that shows active, paused and finished tasks. It's live on Android and iOS; web wasn't confirmed yet.

items.headline: OpenAI stops charging agents for idle sandbox time
items.explainer: Agents built on OpenAI's Agents API run in a hosted sandbox computer, and that is now billed only during active turns, not while the agent waits for you. Sandboxes can also be pre-warmed so replies start faster.

items.headline: Claude can now build live dashboards from your data and animated explainers
items.explainer: Ask a question in plain words and Claude builds a dashboard that stays current, showing the query behind every number. Motion turns a report into a short animation you can export as MP4. Both are in beta on paid plans (Motion on Team and Enterprise).

items.headline: GPT-6 rolls out to everyone in ChatGPT, with interactive answers
items.explainer: ChatGPT answers can now include charts, buttons, forms and small tools you use right in the chat. Paid plans get GPT-6 Sol and Free and Go users get GPT-6 Luna, starting October 8.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5, a fast, cheap model for high-volume bot work
items.explainer: At $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, Anthropic says it costs about 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5. It's built for summaries, sorting and browser use: the simple, repeated jobs most everyday bots do.

items.headline: Anthropic halves Sonnet 5.5 cache reads and gives Max and Team plans monthly API credits
items.explainer: Cached reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 dropped from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, which Anthropic says makes most agent work about 20% cheaper. Max subscribers get $100 or $200 a month in API credits, and Team plans up to $500, to build their own bots.

items.headline: Mistral previews Mistral Large 4, with open weights promised by month's end
items.explainer: Mistral's biggest model yet is in a public preview on its API, and Mistral says anyone will be able to download and run it themselves later this month. That's good news if you want a strong model you can host privately.

items.headline: Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
items.explainer: A Claude sidebar can read the file you have open and edit it in place, asking before each change by default. It's in beta on all paid Claude plans, so your doc-and-spreadsheet chores can go to Claude without copy-pasting.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Sol: near-top performance at a fifth of the price
items.explainer: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches its top model, GPT-6 Astra, on agent work at one-fifth of Astra's token prices ($2 / $10 per million). For bot builders, it's a cheaper middle option for jobs a small model can't handle.

items.headline: OpenAI's Agents API can now use a web browser
items.explainer: Agents built on OpenAI's platform can now complete tasks in an OpenAI-hosted browser, with the app asking you before it visits a site and handling sign-in. Expect more third-party bots that click through websites for you.

items.headline: OpenAI launches dots: always-on agents with their own computer
items.explainer: A dot runs on GPT-6 Astra with its own cloud computer, connects to your apps, and keeps working between chats, checking with you on decisions. It's rolling out to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users first (not the EU, Switzerland or the UK on Pro at launch).

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.explainer: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 runs 30%+ faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less for most work. It's the middle model many agent apps use by default.

items.headline: Grok Bot adds Team Bots: shared AI teammates for a whole team
items.explainer: One person sets up a bot with the files, apps and skills it needs, then the whole team can use it in Slack or Grok Bot, while each person's chats stay private. It's in public beta for Teams and Enterprise plans.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5
items.explainer: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads. It's the model to reach for when a bot's job is hard, not routine.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna
items.explainer: Two new models: Sol for most work and Luna, a very cheap one at $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens. Luna is the kind of model to use for simple, frequent bot jobs.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.7
items.explainer: xAI's new model for coding and knowledge work keeps the same $2 / $6 per million token price as Grok 4.6. xAI says it was trained to work inside the Grok Bot harness, which should make Grok Bot better at everyday tasks.

_impact_rule: Importance, not popularity. major = a new flagship model or a major agent launch from a big lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI). minor = small changelog-level tweaks (a billing detail, a new tool price, a UI move, infrastructure code). notable = everything in between.
